independent_source_risks.title: Performance, historical and recommendation generalizations
independent_source_risks.detail: The 2026 superiority/default claims, 400M comparison, latency figures, 50k/500 thresholds, and historical production dominance lack a specified evaluation protocol. Neither cited opinion nor canonical toy demonstrates universal performance. Medium and the paywalled paper were not consulted; only official technical docs were used.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Ubiquitous does not mean no possible label information
independent_source_risks.detail: A word present in every document can still have informative count patterns. The source uninformative assertion was preserved after the author removed a Chinese weakening. No factual correction was inserted.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Formula and library normalization differ
independent_source_risks.detail: Opening formula uses unsmoothed log(N/df), implementation uses log((N+1)/(df+1))+1 and count/sum(row). scikit-learn default TF uses counts before L2. Per-row scalar TF normalization cancels after L2 for nonzero rows but pre-L2 vectors differ.
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Log does not universally bound IDF
independent_source_risks.detail: For df=1, log(N/df) grows with N; ubiquitous weights are small because N/df is near 1. The source bounded explanation is incomplete, not a generally valid mathematical bound.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Sparsity means zero entries, not small magnitudes
independent_source_risks.detail: The displayed three-document/five-word example has 9 nonzero entries out of 15; most are nonzero. Dense Python lists store all coordinates even when many numerical entries are zero. Small-entry wording is faithfully retained.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Document-length claim conflicts with normalized TF
independent_source_risks.detail: Counts proportional by a positive scalar have identical count/sum(row) TF and, for the same IDF, identical vectors even before L2. Longer documents need not have larger vectors under the source implementation.
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Zero/proportional vector and cosine assumptions
independent_source_risks.detail: Zero rows remain zero and are not on a unit hypersphere. Canonical cosine_similarity is just dot product and requires normalized inputs. Cosine1 also occurs for positive proportional counts, not only identical documents; zero-vector cosine is undefined though code returns0.
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Input and fitting contract omissions
independent_source_risks.detail: First-seen vocabulary order assumes an initial nonempty document. Empty corpus tfidf([]) raises IndexError; empty rows survive. Unknown words are silently dropped, TF denominator counts only retained words, and each tfidf call recomputes IDF rather than exposing a trained fit/transform contract.
independent_source_risks.evidence: finite empty/OOV checks and source inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Dense memory threshold is conditional
independent_source_risks.detail: 100k documents alone cannot establish out-of-memory: memory also depends on vocabulary size, dtype, representation overhead and available hardware. Sparse output advice is useful but the absolute threshold is not universal.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Feature coefficients and stopwords do not guarantee explanations or performance
independent_source_risks.detail: Whether bigrams, filtering and stopwords help is task dependent. A coefficient is not a complete per-document contribution without the feature value, and largest coefficients are not causal explanations. Protected artifact rules are recommendations, not executed instructions.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: BoW cannot recover word proximity from orderless inputs
independent_source_risks.detail: An unigram count representation is invariant under arbitrary token permutations. More training cannot recover whether not is near good from that representation alone, though a classifier can learn presence/co-occurrence and n-grams can change the representation.
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: TF-IDF overlap depends on weighting and tokenization
independent_source_risks.detail: The shared token set is the/movie/was after lowercasing. In a corpus of just these two examples, unsmoothed IDF makes shared coordinates zero, so shared words are not necessarily nonzero TF-IDF overlap. The smoothed formula behaves differently.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: OOV example and remedy depend on tokenizer/model
independent_source_risks.detail: Canonical regex splits Zoomer-approved into zoomer and approved. Whole-token OOV analysis requires a compatible tokenizer. Subword embeddings do not guarantee correct unseen-term semantics, and TF-IDF can also use subword/character features; this source is a fixed word-vocabulary example.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Hybrid repeats document-level term weights per occurrence
independent_source_risks.detail: If tfidf_scores contains per-term TF-IDF already including term frequency, iterating each token occurrence counts frequency again. With a,a,b and weights2/3,1/3 the code returns .8,.2 instead of unique-term weighting2/3,1/3. Static weights as attention is an analogy, not learned context-dependent attention.
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired

independent_source_risks.title: Toy implementation and example boundaries
independent_source_risks.detail: Canonical94-line program vectorizes3 local documents and prints their cosine matrix; it does not train a classifier, implement the hybrid, run sklearn, or evaluate GloVe/20Newsgroups. Safe hybrid definition was checked separately on artificial vectors only. No lesson tests directory exists and the canonical source lacks the repository-required header.
independent_source_risks.evidence: fixed English and full canonical inspection
independent_source_risks.translation_action: Source kept faithful; not silently repaired
